key_insight: CompressionBench studies whether coding agents can autonomously compress pretrained LLMs while preserving their behavior under a smaller storage budget. The supplied abstract is incomplete and does not report performance results.
problem_solved: Tests whether AI agents can turn model compression into an autonomous engineering task while working within storage, inference-environment, and time constraints.
method: Frame LLM compression as a terminal-based task for a coding agent.
Provide a source checkpoint, storage limit, inference environment, and time budget.
Have the agent construct compressed weights, aiming to retain the source model's behavior within the storage limit.
impact: This benchmark could help practitioners assess coding agents for model-efficiency work. It also provides a concrete task for studying whether AI systems can improve the models used by subsequent systems.
visual_elements: Workflow diagram: source checkpoint → coding agent → compressed weights.
Constraint icons representing storage, inference environment, and time budget.
Conceptual trade-off chart showing model storage versus behavior retention, clearly labeled as illustrative.
Feedback-loop diagram connecting autonomous compression to more efficient future AI systems.
paper_title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
paper_authors: Xinrui Zhong, Zhifeng Li, Zhiming Wang, Yongqi Liu, Shanglin Yang
